# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

### Nov 3, 2026
11 7:28a ○ stringifySetCookie currently validates maxAge only as an integer
12 " ○ Existing maxAge tests cover integer validation and negative parsing but not a 400-day ceiling
13 7:29a ◆ stringifySetCookie rejects maxAge above 400 days with a TypeError
S3 Cookie library: make stringifySetCookie reject maxAge over 400 days (34,560,000 seconds) with a TypeError, with tests and README updated (Nov 3, 7:29 AM)
**Investigated**: The cookie repo's maxAge handling in src/index.ts, the README maxAge section, and the existing maxAge tests in src/stringify-set-cookie.spec.ts and src/parse-set-cookie.spec.ts. The stringify path previously checked only that maxAge was an integer, and parse accepted any Max-Age value, including negatives.

**Learned**: stringifySetCookie previously emitted any integer maxAge as "; Max-Age=N" with no upper bound. Browsers cap cookie lifetimes at 400 days, so larger values were silently shortened. Parsing of incoming Max-Age headers is separate and remains unbounded.

**Completed**: src/index.ts now defines a 400-day constant and throws TypeError "option maxAge is too large (max 34560000): <value>" when maxAge exceeds it. The check runs after the integer check. The maxAge JSDoc was updated. The README maxAge section documents the 400-day limit. src/stringify-set-cookie.spec.ts gained tests for 34,560,000 (accepted) and 34,560,001 (throws). The vitest run passed 63,742 tests across 4 files, tsc --noEmit reported no errors, and git diff shows 3 files changed with 27 insertions. Nothing has been committed.

**Next Steps**: No further work is in progress. The changes are uncommitted in the working tree and await review or a commit instruction from the user.

**Notes**: Negative maxAge values are not bounded by this change, and parseSetCookie still accepts any incoming Max-Age value. Only the stringify side enforces the cap, as requested.
